Q: How do I tar a directory without retaining the directory structure? A:

Use the --directory (-C) option specifying the parent-path to suppress and add the path fraction to retain as argument:

tar czf ~/backup.tgz --directory=/home/username/drupal/sites/default files

Q: Deploying React app to production returns "You need to enable JavaScript to run this app" A:

I just looked at the Networks tab, and as you mentioned, the request is being sent to a backend route deployed on Vercel. However, why are you using React for the backend? Couldn't you use Node.js or Express instead? React is primarily a frontend library, whereas Node.js and Express are commonly used for server-side applications. Also, since the introduction of Next.js, React is generally described as a library rather than a framework.

Q: How should a table reference two columns that have a many-to-many relationship? A:

If each product has one brand but can have multiple suppliers, you don't need Products to reference the BrandsSuppliers table.

A simpler design is:

Products
--------
ID
Name
BrandID  -- FK → Brands(ID)

ProductSuppliers
----------------
ProductID   -- FK → Products(ID)
SupplierID  -- FK → Suppliers(ID)

PRIMARY KEY (ProductID, SupplierID)

This directly models the relationships:

  • Product → Brand = many-to-one

  • Product ↔ Supplier = many-to-many

Only use BrandsSuppliers if you specifically need to model which suppliers are associated with which brands independently of individual products.

So, don't add a foreign key to the bridge table just because Brand and Supplier have a many-to-many relationship. The correct design depends on the business relationship you're actually trying to represent.

Q: Can't find the 'libpq-fe.h header when trying to install pg gem A:

It looks like in Ubuntu that header is part of the libpq-dev package (at least in the following Ubuntu versions: 11.04 (Natty Narwhal), 10.04 (Lucid Lynx), 11.10 (Oneiric Ocelot), 12.04 (Precise Pangolin), 14.04 (Trusty Tahr), 18.04 (Bionic Beaver) and 24.04(Noble Numbat):

...
/usr/include/postgresql/libpq-fe.h
...

So try installing libpq-dev or its equivalent for your OS:

  • For Ubuntu/Debian systems: sudo apt-get install libpq-dev
  • On Red Hat Linux (RHEL) systems: yum install postgresql-devel
  • For Mac Homebrew: brew install postgresql
  • For Mac MacPorts PostgreSQL: gem install pg -- --with-pg-config=/opt/local/lib/postgresql[version number]/bin/pg_config
  • For OpenSuse: zypper in postgresql-devel
  • For ArchLinux: pacman -S postgresql-libs

Q: How to read an environment variable in Kotlin? A:

If you're using Kotlin / JVM then you can just use Java's System.getenv() since environment variables are provided by the JVM rather than the Kotlin standard library. For example:
val value = System.getenv("MY_ENV_VAR")

This will return the value of the variable or null if it isn't set. If you want a default value, you can write like this:

val value = System.getenv("MY_ENV_VAR") ? "default"

Q: psexec remote computer name A:

You could also just use the system account to bypass restrictions but as far as the path you can just point to where the script is being run from instead of coping to the local computer then trying to run from there.

psexec @c:\test.txt -s "%~DP0IE10fix.bat"

This pulls from the text and runs as system account (mostly used if you want it to be silent to the user) then runs IE10fix.bat from the location of the batch file your're executing. So you'll have to put the IE10fix.bat in the same location as the .bat running this command.
